newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - OCT 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - OCT 21.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on the front page of its Monday edition:

NASHUA, NEW HAMPSHIRE - Republican nominee Bob Dole proposed a series of restrictions on political fund-raising as Republicans kept the spotlight on what they call the ethical lapses of the Clinton administration.

WASHINGTON - Four years ago, Democrat Bill Clinton mounted an assault on what it described as a pattern of secrecy and dirty tricks by the administration of President George Bush; now Clinton is the lightning rod for character issues.

DENVER - President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore are touting the importance of federal programs geared to women, a sign of the increasing muscle of women voters, who represent about 60 percent of Clinton's support.
FOXBORO, MASSACHUSETTS - Washington's D.C. United soccer team won the Major League Soccer championship in the US, 3-2, in the fourth minute of sudden-death overtime.
TOKYO - Japanese voters restored the country's most conservative party to a near-majority in parliament, taking a step back toward the political order they rejected three years ago.
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's Deputy President Thabo Mbeki is being closely watched as Pretoria's president-in-waiting.
